column1: # `dungeon-mode.md §8.1`'s `J` Jimmy row, which had no capture and, until
# today, no reader in the engine either: the five results - `No keys!`,
# `Key broke!`, `Chest unlocked`, `Already open!`, `What?` - each carry "a
# bare `\n` first, so the result always starts on a new row".
# The party stands on the Shame chest, the second of the shipped file's
# three `0x4?` cells, seeded with
#   seed_position <profile> dungeon=38 level=3 x=1 y=0
# In order: J on the locked chest (a roll - `Chest unlocked` or
# `Key broke!`), O on whatever that left, and J again once the chest is
# open (`Already open!`) or still shut.
# **A lottery below the row level**, like `dungeon-chest`: the pick is a
# `1..30` roll against `(2Z - Dexterity + 30) / 2`, the trap word is the
# shared resolver's draw, and the contents are `containers.md`'s gated
# rows. The shape is what this measures - which literal lands on which
# row, and whether the pick leaves the chest shut.
# **The whole run is also a wandering-monster lottery.** Measured
# 2026-10-16: the seed's active-monster record is all zeros - live, stamped
# level 0, at `(0,0)`, combat class 0 (the Mage) - and a load reuses it whole
# (`dungeon-mode.md §4.1`). `(0,0)` is the cell west of the party, so §14's
# random walk can step straight onto it on the torch's turn: stock printed
# `Attacked from the west!` under `Ignite torch!` and fought three Mages in
# 4 of 9 runs (2026-09-19 14:57 and all three of 2026-10-16), after which
# every beat compares an arena with a dungeon. This engine was attacked in
# none until its stamped-level gate went (headless after the fix: 2 of 10).
# A beat that differs because one side was attacked has measured the walk.
# The row shape itself agrees: the untrapped `0pen-` / `Chest opened` pair
# (no blank row - `\nChest opened\n` after a bare prefix) that read `scroll`
# on 2026-10-14 was fixed before rc1, and the rc1 run's `Key broke!` /
# `0pen-ACID!` / blank / `Chest opened` matches stock's 2026-09-19 15:09 run.
